summary.text: Bruce Westerman is the Republican nominee and incumbent U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 4th District, seeking re-election. An engineer and forester from Hot Springs, he served on a school board and in the Arkansas House of Representatives, including as House Majority Leader, before being elected to Congress in 2014. He chairs the House Natural Resources Committee and also serves on Transportation and Infrastructure.

paragraphs.text: Westerman is a Hot Springs native who, according to his official House biography, graduated from Fountain Lake High School in Garland County and is a husband and father of four.

He attended the University of Arkansas, where he played on the Razorback football team, and earned a bachelor's degree in biological and agricultural engineering in 1990; he later earned a Master of Forestry from Yale University in 2001.
He worked as a plant engineer for Riceland Foods and as an engineer and forester for Mid-South Engineering Company; his House biography says he spent 22 years at Mid-South Engineering in Hot Springs.
Westerman served on the Fountain Lake School Board from 2006 to 2010, including as president in 2009-2010.

He served in the Arkansas House of Representatives from 2011 to 2014, as House Minority Leader (2012-2013) and then House Majority Leader (2013-2014); his House biography says he was the state's first Republican House Majority Leader since Reconstruction.
Westerman won election to the U.S. House in 2014, succeeding Tom Cotton, and has served since January 2015.
He serves on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and is chairman of the Committee on Natural Resources.
